G21300:
φαλακρόομαι φα^λακρόομαι,
Pass. to become bald, Hdt.
[from φα^λακρός]
G21305:
φειδώ φειδώ, όος, [φείδομαι]
I. a sparing, νεκύων Il.
II. absol. thrift, parsimony, Od., Hes.: thrift in exposing oneself to danger, Thuc.
G21306:
φθειριάω φθειριάω, φυτ. ‐άσω
to have morbus pedicularis, Plut.
G21307:
φιλανθρωπέω φι^λανθρωπέω, φυτ. ‐ήσω [from φιλ/ανθρωπος]
to treat humanely, Polyb.
G21309:
φιλαρχία φι^λαρχία, ἡ,
love of rule, lust of power, Theophr., Plut.
G21312:
φιλογύνης φι^λογύ^νης, ου, ὁ,
fond of women, pl. φιλογύναικες Plat.
G21313:
φιλοπολίτης φι^—λο‐πολίτης, ου, ὁ,
loving one's fellow-citizens, Plut.
G21315:
φιλόψυχος φι^λό‐ψυ—χος, ον, [ψυχή]
loving one's life, cowardly, dastardly, faint-hearted, Eur.
G21318:
φοιβάω φοιβάω, φυτ. ‐ήσω [φοῖβος]
to cleanse, purify, Theocr.
G21322:
φρενόω φρενόω, φυτ. ‐ώσω [φρήν]
I. to make wise, instruct, inform, teach, τινά Trag., Xen.; φρενώσω δ’ οὐκέτ’ ἐξ αἰνιγμάτων, i. e. will teach plainly, Aesch.
II. in Pass. to be elated, Babr.
G21328:
φυτός φυ^τός, ή, όν [verb. adj. of φύω]
shaped by nature, without art, Pind.
G21333:
χαροπός χα^ρ‐οπός, ή, όν [χαρά, ὤψ]
1. glad-eyed, bright-eyed, χαροποὶ λέοντες Od., Hes.; θῆρες Soph.:—later, it denoted light-blue or grayish colour, ὄμματά μοι γλαυκᾶς χαροπώτερα πολλὸν Ἀθάνας Theocr.; also of the Germans, v. χαροπότης.
2. of the eyes of youths, sparkling with joy, joyous, gladsome, Theocr., Anth.
G21335:
χείμαρος χείμα^ρος, ὁ, [χεῖμα]
a plug in a ship's bottom, drawn out when the ship was brought on land, to let out the bilge-water, Hes.
G21336:
χειρονομία χειρονομία, ἡ,
gesticulation, Luc.
G21343:
χοανεύω χοα^νεύω,
I. to cast into a mould (χοάνος), Ar.
II. to cast metal:—Pass., κεχωνευμένος Plut.
[from χοά^νη]
G21346:
χοῦς
I. Lat. congius, a liquid measure = 12 κοτύλαι, nearly 3 quarts, Ar., etc.
2. proverb. of attempts to measure the immeasurable, οἱ τῆς θαλάττης λεγόμενοι χόες Plat.
II. Χόες, οἱ, the Pitcher-feast, the second day of the Anthesteria at Athens, Ar., Dem.

χοῦς
1. earth thrown down or heaped up, like χῶμα, Hdt.
2. = κονιορτός, dust, NTest.
G21347:
χρηματιστήριον χρημα^τιστήριον, ου, τό, [χρηματίζω]
a place for transacting business, a counting-house, Plut.
G21348:
χρησιμεύω χρησι^μεύω,
to be useful or serviceable, τινί to one, Luc.
G21352:
χυλός χυ—λός, οῦ, ὁ, [χέω]
juice, esp. juice produced by decoction or digestion:—metaph., χυλὸν διδοὺς στωμυλμάτων administering a decoction of small talk, Ar.; χ. φιλίας id.
G21355:
ψάμμος ψάμμος, ἡ,
I. sand, so called from its loose, crumbling nature (from ψάω), Od., etc.:—proverb., ψάμμος ἀριθμὸν περιπέφευγεν Pind.
II. ἡ ψ. the sandy desert of Libya, Hdt.
[Both ψάμμος and ψάμαθος sometimes drop ψ and become ἄμμος, ἄμαθος.]
G21357:
ψάω [cf. καταψάω]
I. to touch lightly, rub;
II. intr. to crumble away, vanish, disappear, Soph.
G21361:
ψίθυρος ψί^θυ^ρος, ον,
I. whispering: slanderous, Soph.
II. as Subst., ψίθυρος, = ψιθυριστής, a whisperer, slanderer, Pind.
2. twittering, of birds, Anth.
[Perh. formed from the sound.]
G21363:
ψυχαγωγία [from ψυ—χα^γωγέω] ψυ—χα^γωγία, ἡ,
a winning of souls, persuasion, Plat.
G21365:
ὠδίς ὠδίς, ῖνος, ἡ, [mostly in pl.]
I. the pangs or throes of labour, travail-pains, Il.; ἐν μόναις ὠδῖσιν at a single birth, Pind.; ἐν ὠδίνων ἀνάγκαις Eur.; in sg. travail-pain, anguish, Pind., Soph.
2. in sg., also, the fruit of travail or labour, a birth, child, Aesch., Eur.; ἄπτερον ὠδῖνα τέκνων, of young birds, Eur.
II. metaph. any travail, anguish, Aesch.; also in pl., of love, pangs, Soph., Plat.
G21366: ὤμιον [Dim. of ὦμος, Anth.]
G21367:
ὠμότης ὠμότης, ητος, ἡ, [ὠμός]
rawness: metaph. savageness, fierceness, cruelty, Eur., Xen., etc.
G21368:
ὠμόφρων ὠμό‐φρων, ονος, ὁ, ἡ, [φρήν]
savage-minded, savage, Trag. adv. ὠμοφρόνως, Aesch.
G21370:
πλάνης πλά^νης, ητος, ὁ,
I. a wanderer, roamer, rover, Soph., Eur.
2. πλάνητες ἀστέρες the planets, Xen.
II. as adj. wandering, Plut.
G21372:
ἁδρόομαι [ἁδρός]
to come to one's strength, Plat.
G21374:
ἀκαρπία [ἄκαρπος]
unfruitfulness, barrenness, Aesch.
G21377:
ἀνεπιεικής
unreasonable, unfair, Thuc.
G21378:
ἀνθαιρέομαι
I. Dep.:— to choose one person or thing instead of another, τινά (or τί) τινος Eur.; to prefer, choose rather, id.
II. to dispute, lay claim to, τι id.
G21379:
ἄοκνος
without hesitation, untiring, Hes., Soph., Thuc.
G21380:
ἀπαυτομολέω
to go of one's own accord, desert, Thuc.
G21381:
ἀπογιγνώσκω
I. depart from a judgment, give up a design or intention of doing, ἀπ. τὸ μάχεσθαι Xen.; ἀπ. μὴ βοηθεῖν to resolve not to help, Dem.
II. c. gen. rei, to despair of a thing, c. gen., Lys.:—absol. to despair, Dem.
2. c. acc. to give up as hopeless, id.:—Pass. to be so given up, Dem.
III. as law-term, to refuse to receive an accusation, reject, id.:— ἀπ. τινος (sc. δίκην vel γραφήν) to reject the charge brought against a man, i. e. acquit him, opp. to καταγιγνώσκειν τινός, id.: also, ἀπ. τινά (sc. τῆς δίκης vel γραφῆς) to judge one free from the accusation, to acquit him, id.
G21384:
ἀποτρίβω
I. to wear out, Od.
II. to rub clean, to rub down a horse, Xen.
III. to rub off, Theocr.:—Mid. to get rid of, Dem., Aeschin.: to decline, reject, τὴν πεῖραν Plut.
G21385:
ἀσμενίζω [ἄσμενος]
to be well-pleased, Polyb.
G21386:
βαπτός [from βάπτω]
I. dipped, dyed, bright-coloured, Ar.
2. for dyeing, χρώματα Plat.
II. of water, drawn by dipping vessels (cf. βάπτω I. 3), Eur.
G21387:
βουγάιος [γαίω]
a great bully or braggart, voc. βουγάϊε Hom.
G21388:
διαβάθρα [βαίνω]
a ship's ladder, Luc.
G21391:
δίνη δί—νη, ἡ,
1. a whirlpool, eddy, Lat. vortex, Il., etc.
2. a whirlwind, Ar.
3. generally, a whirling, rotation, id., Plat.: metaph., ἀνάγκης δίναι Aesch.
G21394:
ἐκπρεπής ἐκπρεπής, ές [ἐκπρέπω]
I. distinguished out of all, preeminent, remarkable, Il.; μεγέθει ἐκπρεπεστάτα Aesch.; εἶδος ἐκπρεπεστάτη Eur.
II. = ἔξω τοῦ πρέποντος, unseemly, monstrous, Thuc.: so adv. ‐πῶς, without reasonable grounds, id.
G21395:
ἐκτίνω fut. ‐τίσω aor1 ἐξέτι—σα
I. to pay off, pay in full, Hdt., attic;— δίκην ἐκτ. to pay full penalty, Eur.; τινός for a thing, Hdt.
II. Mid. to exact full payment for a thing, avenge, c. acc. rei, Soph., Eur.; to take vengeance on, τινά id.
G21398:
ἔνοικος ἔν‐οικος,
1. in-dwelling: an inhabitant, Trag., Thuc., etc.
2. pass. dwelt in, Eur.
